definition: the branch of mathematics in which letters stand for unknown numbers
hook: Algebra was a word for setting broken bones before it was a word for mathematics.
modernAnchor: A letter standing in for a number, a sheet of homework, x on both sides. We call it algebra.
journey: Around the year 820 the Baghdad scholar al-Khwarizmi wrote a book on solving equations, and called his method al-jabr.
The verb behind it, jabara, meant to restore or to set something broken, the way a surgeon sets a bone.
He meant it as a picture. An equation with terms stranded on the wrong side is a thing out of joint, and you put it back together.
The older sense travelled too. In Don Quixote an algebrista is not a mathematician but the man who sets the bone.
